claims.quote: Battles will last for days, and at the end it is very doubtful whether any decisive victory can be gained.
claims.description: Future battles will last for days because trench digging is slow, and may end without a decisive victory.

claims.quote: There will be no war in the future
claims.description: Modern war will become impossible because it would mean suicide for the states that wage it.

claims.quote: In reality the war of the future, if ever it takes place, will not be fighting ; it will be terminated by famine.
claims.description: Future wars will be decided by starving the populations rather than by fighting.

claims.quote: The first thing to be borne in mind is that the next war will be a long war.
claims.description: The next major war will be a long one, with no decisive result possible in under two years.

claims.quote: to take a modern fortress adequately defended, even by superior forces, is an operation which cannot be put through in less than one hundred and twenty days
claims.description: Taking a modern, well-defended fortress will require at least 120 days of siege.

claims.quote: In two weeks' time after the French army is mobilised, it is the expectation of the best authorities that they would have 100,000 men in hospital, even if never a shot had been fired.
claims.description: Within two weeks of mobilization a French army will have 100,000 men in hospital from illness, without any fighting.
claims.stated_time: in two weeks' time after the French army is mobilised

claims.quote: It is estimated that if a body of 10,000 men, advancing to the attack, had to traverse a distance of a mile and a half under the fire of a single battery, they would be exposed to 1450 rounds before they crossed the zone of fire
claims.description: An attacking column of 10,000 men crossing a mile and a half under one battery would face 1450 shells.

claims.quote: the war would not last many weeks before the majority of the officers had been killed off.
claims.description: In a modern war most officers would be killed within a few weeks of the start.

claims.quote: Hence, under modern conditions of warfare every army will tend inevitably to degenerate into such a mob.
claims.description: Modern armies that lose their officers will inevitably degenerate into cowardly mobs.

claims.quote: Now the whole line of communications will be exposed to dropping shots from marksmen who, from the security of thicket or hedge, will deal out sudden death without any tell-tale smoke to guide their exasperated and harassed enemy to the hidingplace.
claims.description: Smokeless powder lets snipers hidden in hedges pick off enemy supply lines without revealing their position.

claims.quote: There will be practically no care for the wounded
claims.description: Wounded soldiers in future wars will be left where they fall, since rescuers cannot reach them under fire.

claims.quote: What is much more likely to be done is that the dying and the dead will be utilised as ramparts to strengthen the shelter trenches.
claims.description: Dead and dying soldiers will be piled up as ramparts to shelter the living in trenches.

claims.quote: everybody will be entrenched in the next war
claims.description: Every soldier in the next war will dig trenches first to survive, making battlefields like sieges.

claims.quote: It is much more probable that in the future both sides will claim the victory.
claims.description: Future wars will end with both sides claiming victory rather than one clear winner.

claims.quote: In a war between the Triple and the Dual Alliance there would be ten millions of men under arms.
claims.description: A war between the Triple and Dual Alliances would mobilize about ten million men.

claims.quote: armies will empty their magazines, and the army that fires its last cartridge first will be at the mercy of the other
claims.description: With rapid-fire weapons, armies may run out of ammunition, leaving whoever fires its last cartridge first at the mercy of its foe.
